title: Optimize host submission queue and memory-copy paths to reduce CPU-GPU stalls
creator: Arjun Mehta
description: Problem: Observed tail latency and degraded throughput for small and medium-sized requests due to host-side stalls. Root causes include frequent host->device memory copies, bursty kernel submissions with blocking synchronization points, and contention inside the host threadpool used for prefill/submit tasks. This ticket aims to reduce CPU-GPU pipeline overhead by improving submission batching, reusing page-locked buffers, coalescing events, and making the host scheduler NUMA-aware.
acceptance_criteria: P50 and P95 token-latency for short (<= 64 tokens) generation workloads reduced by >= 20% in CI perf harness compared to baseline (2026-02-01) for mPT-like models
Host CPU utilization during steady-state serving reduced by at least 15% for mixed traffic profiles
No regression in end-to-end correctness; outputs identical within floating noise compared to baseline when running same seeds and model revision
Feature gated and configurable via runtime flags; default behavior safe for existing customers
Benchmarked on dedicated and hosted configurations; results documented in perf dashboard and PR
implementation_notes: Introduce a submission queue abstraction: batch kernel launches and memory uploads per-GPU per-worker interval (configurable window 0-4ms). Use a single non-blocking submit thread per-GPU to amortize syscall and synchronization overhead.
Implement a page-locked buffer pool with per-NUMA partitioning so host threads can reuse pinned buffers without cross-socket copies. Expose pool sizes via runtime config and monitor allocations.

Replace frequent cudaMemcpy (synchronous) calls in host path with cudaMemcpyAsync into pinned buffers and use CUDA events for lightweight synchronization. Fall back to synchronous copies on devices without async-copy support.
Add an optional zero-copy path for workloads where model weights and activations are already in GPU memory (use GPU-GPU copy or IPC handles), guarded by capability detection.
Tune host threadpool: limit parallel prefill workers based on NUMA locality, add cooperative backoff to avoid thread oversubscription, and move long-running tasks to dedicated I/O threads.
Coalesce attention KV-prefetch tasks where adjacent requests share prefixes: detect common prefixes at scheduler and merge uploads for first N layers.
Add telemetry events for submission queue length, buffer-pool hit rate, pinned-memory allocations, and per-thread stall times for correlation in Console.
Expose experimental flags: runtime.host_submission_window_ms, runtime.pinned_pool_size_mb, runtime.coalesce_prefixes_enabled
experiments: A/B test: submission_window_ms=0 (baseline) vs 2ms window yields ~18% P95 improvement in small-batch gen in initial runs
Pinned pool: 1GB vs 4GB pool per-socket shows diminishing returns after ~3GB; tune defaults to 3GB on 48GB hosts
Threadpool: NUMA-aware vs naive pool reduces cross-socket memory traffic by ~22% and increases overall throughput
Zero-copy path for IPC models reduced host cycles by ~30% but requires additional validation on multi-tenant hosts
risks: Pinned memory over-allocation could starve host processes on multi-tenant hosts—introduce caps and OOM-safeguards
Coalescing prefixes may increase latency for unique requests if merge window too long; must keep window conservative and observable
Async copy path depends on CUDA driver features; need robust capability detection and safe fallback
New submission thread introduces complexity in shutdown and error handling; must ensure deterministic cleanup to avoid GPU hangs
